title_en: The Obligation to Support the Resistance in Palestine
body_ar: استضافت قناة الجزيرة مباشر مساء أمس الأحد 29 رمضان 1435هـ الموافق 27 يوليو 2014هـ فضيلة الشيخ محـمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بموريتانيا؛ و قد تحدث فضيلة الشيخ عن أهمية فلسطين و وجوب نصرة أهلها و أن الجهاد باق إلى يوم القيامة لا ينكره من يؤمن بالله و اليوم الآخر مبينا أن على الأمة أن تلتف حول مقاومتها و أن تناصرها و أن لا تبخل عليها بالمال و الدعاء مبينا أن دور الأمة في هذه المرحلة يتمثل في بذل المال و الدعاء و المناصرة بالمواقف و أن على حكام الأمة الإسلامية أن ينصروا الله في إخوتهم في غزة و ألا يخذلوهم فإن الله سائلهم عنهم يوم القيامة؛ وفي إطار جوابه على سؤال يتعلق بإمكانية تسليم المقاومة سلاحها، قال فضيلة الشيخ إن الحكام الفاسدين هم الذين عليهم أن يسلموا أسلحتهم ما داموا يخذلون غزة، مضيفا " أما المقاومون فهم الذين يموتون دون أسلحتهم كما كان الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم يفعلون، وأكد فضيلة الشيخ أن على المسلمين أن يهتموا بمختلف قضايا الأمة الإسلامية وأن يكونوا نصرة للمستضعفين في كل مكان، وأن لا تنشغل كل دولة بواقعها ووضعها على حدة، و في إطار حديثه عما يقدمه المسلمون من تبرعات قال فضيلة الشيخ ما يقدمه المسلمون من مساعدات لأهل غزة ليس من باب الصدقة وإنما يمثل نصرة لدين الله تعالى، مبينا أنه لا بد لكل مسلم أن يشارك بماله وكل ما يملك نصرة لدين الله، وأن على الناس أن يدركوا أن المساعدات التي قدموا لغزة ستصلها و تكون لها عونا و نصرا بإذن الله .
body_en:
Al Jazeera Mubasher hosted, yesterday evening, Sunday 29 Ramadan 1435 AH, corresponding to 27 July 2014, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Mauritania.

The Sheikh spoke about the importance of Palestine and the obligation to support its people, and that jihad remains until the Day of Resurrection and is not denied by anyone who believes in God and the Last Day. He explained that the community must rally around its resistance, support it, and not be sparing towards it with money and supplication; explaining that the community's part at this stage consists in the giving of money, in supplication, and in support through the positions it takes; and that the rulers of the Muslim community must support God in the matter of their brothers in Gaza and must not abandon them, for God will question them about them on the Day of Resurrection.

In the course of his answer to a question about the possibility of the resistance handing over its weapons, the Sheikh said that it is the corrupt rulers who ought to hand over their weapons, so long as they abandon Gaza; adding: "As for those who resist, they are the ones who die rather than give up their weapons, as the Companions (may God be pleased with them) used to do."

The Sheikh affirmed that Muslims must concern themselves with the various causes of the Muslim community and be a support to the oppressed everywhere, and that each state must not be taken up with its own circumstances and situation in isolation.

Speaking of the donations Muslims give, the Sheikh said that what Muslims provide in aid to the people of Gaza is not a matter of voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), but represents support for the religion of God the Exalted; explaining that every Muslim must take part with his wealth and everything he possesses in support of God's religion, and that people must realise that the aid they have offered to Gaza will reach it and will be a help and a support to it, God willing.

flags.arabic: إن الحكام الفاسدين هم الذين عليهم أن يسلموا أسلحتهم ما داموا يخذلون غزة
flags.context: the Sheikh's reply to a question about the resistance handing over its weapons
flags.note: EDITORIAL, HIGH. The record reports the Sheikh saying, on satellite television, that jihad continues until the Day of Resurrection; that the community must rally around the Palestinian resistance and fund it; that Muslim rulers who abandon Gaza are corrupt and are the ones who should disarm; and that those who resist die rather than surrender their weapons. Translated faithfully — neither softened nor strengthened — as style guide section 12 requires. In English these sentences are material that some jurisdictions treat as support for a proscribed organisation, and publishing them carries real legal and reputational exposure for Ummah Collective as well as for the Sheikh. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office and must be taken consciously, not by default.

flags.arabic: مضيفا " أما المقاومون فهم الذين يموتون دون أسلحتهم كما كان الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم يفعلون،
flags.context: the one directly quoted sentence in the record
options: the closing quotation mark is missing and the quotation may run further
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): the quotation is opened and never closed; the sentence that follows begins a new report in the site's voice, which is why the quotation has been closed at يفعلون in the English. If more of what follows was also his direct wording, that cannot be recovered from the record. This matters, because it is the only sentence in the piece presented as his own words.

flags.context: المقاومون فهم الذين يموتون دون أسلحتهم
options: die rather than give up their weapons
die in defence of their weapons
flags.note: دون here is the classical 'in defence of' or 'rather than surrender', as in the report about dying دون ماله. The third reading, 'without their weapons', is grammatically available and gives the opposite sense; it is excluded by the context of the question about disarming, but the ambiguity is recorded.

flags.context: the date given in the first sentence
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): the Hijri marker هـ is attached to a Gregorian year. Preserved in body_ar; the English gives the date without the marker.

flags.arabic: أن ينصروا الله في إخوتهم في غزة
flags.context: the Sheikh's charge to Muslim rulers
options: support God in the matter of their brothers in Gaza
give victory to God in respect of their brothers in Gaza
aid God's cause in their brothers in Gaza
flags.note: نصر الله is the Qur'anic idiom (إن تنصروا الله ينصركم, Sūrat Muḥammad 47:7) and the English keeps its strangeness rather than flattening it into 'help the people of Gaza', which is not what the Arabic says. The verse is not cited in the record and has not been supplied in the text.

translator_notes: A news report of a television appearance, not a transcript, and only one sentence is presented as direct quotation. Everything else is the site's summary of what he said, and the English must not be cited as his wording.
The title, 'The Obligation to Support the Resistance in Palestine', is the site's headline, not a fatwa heading; the record is filed under news and is not a written fatwa.
صدقة is rendered by its glossary value, 'voluntary charity'. The Sheikh's point turns on the contrast: he denies that the aid falls under that heading.
dec: Reports a call to rally around and fund the Palestinian resistance. Treated in some jurisdictions as support for a proscribed organisation.
